correctness.rationale: The complex consists precisely of subsets of full tilings. Independently enumerate bijections from black to white vertices, retain the 36 supported by grid edges, and take all subsets; this gives 5,407 faces including the empty face. Rather than replaying the collapse calculation, form signed orbit-sum bases on each augmented rational chain group for each cyclic subgroup generated by representatives 1,r,r^2,s,rs. An orbit with negative total sign has no invariant generator; the other orbits contribute one. The boundaries commute with the action, and the coefficient at the chosen face representative determines the orbit-sum coefficient. Exact sparse rational elimination, with consecutive products checked, gives respective invariant homology dimensions (H2,H3)=(2,1),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,0), and zero in all other reduced degrees. Averaging commutes with homology. An involution has trace 2 times its fixed dimension minus the total dimension; a quarter-turn has trace 2 times its fixed dimension minus the fixed dimension of its square (the i and -i eigenvalues have equal multiplicity). The resulting traces are (2,0,-2,0,0) and (1,-1,1,1,-1), identifying E and eta in the stated reflection convention. Rational characters determine these semisimple modules. After barycentric subdivision stabilizers of simplices act pointwise, so rational quotient chains identify with coinvariants, and averaging gives invariants. Both modules have zero D4-invariants, proving precisely rational acyclicity. The frozen proof's separate method is also sound: unique immediate coface forces a free facet; collapse projection adds a multiple of the free-coface boundary to eliminate the free-face coefficient, then discards the matched coface. The signed trace on the unreduced face groups with the degree-minus-one term included gives the reduced Lefschetz trace.
residual_risks: The rational calculation does not establish integral acyclicity, freeness of the geometric action, or contractibility of the quotient.

value.rationale: The square grid is the natural dihedral test case, and the previously known mixed-dimensional wedge makes both homology groups nontrivial tests for symmetry. The full modules distinguish the action from arbitrary wedge actions and show that all rational reduced homology disappears in the full square quotient, sharply unlike the ordinary matching complex. These data can serve as an exact equivariant benchmark without asserting an integral or general-family result.
residual_risks: No classification of other grids or other coefficient rings.
